Priya (PM): Quick heads-up — we need to triage the incoming customer asks for the Optimize toolkit and lock pilot acceptance criteria by Friday. Too many scope asks: batching heuristics, prefix caching UX, quant recommendation flags, eval-triggered alerts. Can we do a short inventory and prioritization rubric here?
Marco (Eng): +1. Quick ask: which of these are blocked by runtime work (KV cache changes / continuous batching)? I can get rough effort estimates if we scope features smaller.
Elena (ML): From an ML side, quant recommendations need an evaluation harness and perf guardrails. Also need to define acceptable quality delta (e.g., <= 1% concordance drop on eval set).
Maya (CS): Customers (two large SaaS, one fintech) are pushing for: 1) clear quant recommendations per model/hardware, 2) eviction policies for prefix caching, 3) alerts when eval metrics regress. They'd pay for early access.
Jamie (Design): We should separate UX surface for recommendations vs. auto-apply. For pilot keep it read-only: "suggested profile" + explanation.
Priya (PM): Proposed triage rubric: impact (token $ saved / latency improvement), risk (quality regressions), effort (eng + infra), and observability (can we measure/concordance?). Rank highest = pilot scope. Thoughts?
Ravi (Research): Suggest adding "determinism of improvement" — how often recommendation actually yields net econ win across customers. For quantization, that's model + prompt-dependent. We should capture distributional signals.
Marco (Eng): Practical scoping suggestion for pilot (90 days):
- Batching: expose adaptive batch-size suggestion + one opt-in runtime mode for continuous batching (no KV changes).
- Caching: implement simple prefix cache with LRU + dashboard metrics and a knob for TTL.
- Quant recs: run offline sweep + provide per-model recommended quant profile (read-only).
- Eval alerts: one eval pipeline that can trigger slack + email when concordance drops > X on target prompt set.
Elena (ML): For concordance threshold, propose baseline: 95% match on customer-provided eval set OR <= 1.5% absolute drop on internal eval depending on metric. Need to flag false positives.
Maya (CS): For priority: customers want quant recs > caching > batching > eval-alerts in terms of revenue impact. But risk appetite: fintech wants explicit audit trail and rollout controls for quant changes.
Priya (PM): So pilot acceptance criteria (draft):
- Quant recs: recommendations generated for top 3 models, with metrics (latency, token-savings, eval-concordance) visible; at least one customer signs up for read-only pilot.
- Caching: prefix caching produces >=5% token-savings on pilot workload or explain why not, with telemetry and TTL controls.
- Batching: adaptive batch suggestion demonstrates >=10% cost improvement in batchable workloads without increasing p95 beyond SLO.
- Eval alerts: alerts fire with <= 20% FP rate on pilot eval sets and documented mitigation steps.
Marco (Eng): Impl notes: we need schema for recommendation objects — minimal proposal below (will extend):
```
{
  "model": "gpt-open-7b",
  "profile": "int8-qat",
  "expected_token_savings_pct": 12.3,
  "expected_latency_change_ms": 23,
  "concordance_change_pct": -0.4,
  "confidence": "high",
  "rationale": "observed stable perf on eval set with low dispersion"
}
```
Elena (ML): That looks fine. Add "eval_dataset_id" and "timestamp" for audit. Also include percentiles for latency delta, not just mean.
Sam (SRE): Observability checklist: must emit per-request tags for recommendation-used, quant-profile, cache-hit; trace context to connect token-cost reduction to SLOs. If we can't attach tags cheaply, pilot becomes noisy.
Priya (PM): Good call. We'll add observability as a gating criterion. Also need product feature gating: read-only vs auto-apply. Pilot must be read-only.
Maya (CS): I'll surface this to the two anchor customers and check if they can commit pilot data + eval prompts. If they can't, we fallback to synthetic sim.
Ravi (Research): For eval-alerts, suggest we allow a "grace window" rule: alert only if regression persists for N consecutive runs or exceeds delta for M prompts to reduce alerts churn.
Jamie (Design): UX: alert card should show top affected prompt examples + quick rollback button (if auto-apply later). For pilot, show "investigate" button linking to traces.
Marco (Eng): Estimated rough effort (T-shirt):
- Batching single opt-in runtime: M (2-3 sprint dev + infra)
- Prefix cache (simple LRU + metrics): S-M (2 sprints)
- Quant recs offline sweep + UI: M-L (3-4 sprints, research + validation)
- Eval-alert plumbing: S (1-2 sprints)
Priya (PM): Prioritization vote (emoji): React with :one: for quant recs first, :two: for caching first, :three: for batching first, :four: for eval-alerts first. I'll consolidate tomorrow and draft the pilot PRD.
Maya (CS): :one: from me (quant recs).
Elena (ML): :one: and :four: (quant + eval-alerts together ideally).
Marco (Eng): :two: — caching reduces token spend quickly and is lower risk for runtime.
Sam (SRE): :three: (batching) — infrastructure leverage.
Priya (PM): Thanks. Action items:
- Maya: confirm anchor customer willingness + get eval prompt sets by Wed.
- Marco: validate runtime effort estimates and blockers by Tue.
- Elena/Ravi: define concordance metric and threshold proposal by Wed.
- Sam: draft observability event schema and tags by Tue.
- Jamie: sketch alert + recommendation UI flows by Thu.
I'll collect replies and publish a trimmed PRD by Friday for review. ops-bot: deploy reminder scheduled for 2026-03-25 09:00 UTC.
Maya (CS): noted, pinged customer A, they said yes to pilot but need SOC2 assurance in contract.
Marco (Eng): Blocking item: if KV cache change is required later we'll need a migration plan; tracker created (ENG-9876).
Elena (ML): I'll run a small sanity run on internal models this week and post numbers.
Priya (PM): Great — thanks everyone. We'll reconvene Wed standup if anything surprises. :thumbsup:
